items.prose: Ozone gas generated by electrostatic air filters in Intake Plenum 3 caused severe atmospheric crazing across the chloroprene rubber face seals. Deep transverse fissures formed along the chin cup, causing the respirator to fail negative-pressure leak tests.

Decades in dry storage caused di-octyl phthalate plasticizer to weep to the surface as an oily film. The transparent PVC hood lost all flexibility, cracking into razor-sharp shards when unfolded for emergency evacuation drills.

Un-vulcanized free sulfur in natural rubber straps migrated to the outer surface, forming a powdery yellow-white crystalline bloom. The acidic crust caused severe contact dermatitis and ulcerations on dweller cheeks during eight-hour sentry shifts.

Diesel generator exhaust fumes drawn into the decontamination lock softened the thin silicone exhalation valve discs. The elastomeric flaps absorbed aromatic hydrocarbons, curling 3mm off their plastic seats and allowing contaminated air backflow on inhalation.

Repeated high-dose beta decontamination sweeps (cumulative 80 Gy) induced polymer chain cross-linking in the butyl gloves. The rubber hardened from 40 Shore A to 85 Shore D; scouts could no longer bend their fingers to cock rifle hammers.

High relative humidity (95%) and human sweat in Bunkhouse 2 promoted colonization by *Aspergillus* mold. The fungi hydrolyzed the ester linkages in the open-cell foam, reducing forehead pads to a sticky, tar-like black paste that smelled of rot.

Daily washing in 5% sodium hypochlorite bleach solution oxidized the 0.2mm bromobutyl speech diaphragm. Chemical embrittlement produced microscopic radial pinholes around the clamping ring, admitting radioactive radon daughter particulates directly into the mouth cavity.

Sentry patrols during a -38°C nuclear winter blizzard pushed Viton rubber gaskets below their glass transition temperature (-20°C). The seal turned rigid as phenolic resin; an inhale pulled the stiff edge away from the sentry's temple, sucking in freezing ash.
